rationale_evidence.statement: Justifies each context-map edge: Governance->Knowledge (governance establishes what is organizationally binding, e.g. Architecture Decision->Authoritative Knowledge, Governance Policy->Applicable Constraint, Approved Exception->Effective Expected State; governance must not depend on an agent's interpretation to become authoritative); Knowledge->Assurance (knowledge translates governance into reusable engineering meaning, e.g. Decision D42 establishing 'Service X must use pattern P' becomes an assurance expectation, so assurance consumes the authoritative expectation rather than inventing it); Assurance->EngineeringState (assurance observes/evaluates engineering reality but does not own it); Engineering->Evidence (Runtime->Observation->Evidence, e.g. Git commit/CI result/deployed image/Kubernetes state/monitoring/security scan, with KnowledgeOS preserving references/interpretation without becoming the source system); Evidence->Knowledge (Evidence->Claim is valid, but Evidence ↛ Authority automatically — 'one of the central boundaries'), closing the semantic feedback loop Governance->Knowledge->Assurance->Engineering->Evidence->Knowledge.

## Rationale

- [S1028] types=[FORMALIZATION, PRINCIPLE] scope=THEORY-LEVEL — "States the Context Map's purpose is to determine where semantic authority is located and which direction knowledge/dependencies may flow, aiming to prevent the dangerous inversion Technical implementation -> Organizational authority in favor of Authority->Knowledge->Assurance->Engineering->Observation->Evidence with feedback through governed mechanisms; presents the full candidate context-map diagram (Governance[Policy/Decision] -governs/authorizes-> Knowledge[Claims/Facts] -expected state-> Assurance[Rules/Checks] -verifies-> Engineering/Runtime/External Systems -observations-> Evidence -supports-> back to Knowledge), explicitly a target hypothesis, not current-state fact." (anchor: "Authority → Knowledge → Assurance → Engineering → Observation → Evidence")
- [S1028] types=[ANALYSIS] scope=CROSS-OBJECT — "Justifies each context-map edge: Governance->Knowledge (governance establishes what is organizationally binding, e.g. Architecture Decision->Authoritative Knowledge, Governance Policy->Applicable Constraint, Approved Exception->Effective Expected State; governance must not depend on an agent's interpretation to become authoritative); Knowledge->Assurance (knowledge translates governance into reusable engineering meaning, e.g. Decision D42 establishing 'Service X must use pattern P' becomes an assurance expectation, so assurance consumes the authoritative expectation rather than inventing it); Assurance->EngineeringState (assurance observes/evaluates engineering reality but does not own it); Engineering->Evidence (Runtime->Observation->Evidence, e.g. Git commit/CI result/deployed image/Kubernetes state/monitoring/security scan, with KnowledgeOS preserving references/interpretation without becoming the source system); Evidence->Knowledge (Evidence->Claim is valid, but Evidence ↛ Authority automatically — 'one of the central boundaries'), closing the semantic feedback loop Governance->Knowledge->Assurance->Engineering->Evidence->Knowledge." (anchor: "Governance → Knowledge.")
- [S1028] types=[DISTINCTION, FORMALIZATION] scope=CROSS-OBJECT — "Resolves where Finding belongs: Assurance owns Detection (Assurance->FindingDetected), Governance owns Disposition (Finding->Governance), avoiding mixing technical verification with organizational decision-making; gives the Finding lifecycle Assurance->FindingDetected->Classification->Governance->{Remediate, AcceptRisk, Exception, Investigate, FalsePositive}, noting classification may be partly automated but must follow governed rules." (anchor: "Assurance owns Detection; Governance owns Disposition.")
- [S1028] types=[WARNING, PRINCIPLE] scope=CROSS-OBJECT — "Warns against making Evidence a large Shared Kernel across Governance/Knowledge/Assurance/Engineering (creates coupling); prefers Evidence as an owned context consumed by others through references/projections; if a shared kernel is used at all it should be extremely small — potentially only Identity+Reference+Version+ProvenanceMetadata, never the entire Knowledge domain." (anchor: "Evidence as an owned semantic context with explicit contracts ... not a Shared Kernel.")
- [S1028] types=[FORMALIZATION] scope=CROSS-OBJECT — "Proposes a candidate Published Language (named integration-event contracts) whose importance is that the contract carries meaning, not merely technical DTOs." (anchor: "GovernanceDecisionApproved, GovernanceExceptionGranted, KnowledgePublished, EvidenceCaptured, FindingDetected, VerificationCompleted.")
- [S1028] types=[PRINCIPLE, EXAMPLE] scope=CROSS-OBJECT — "Elaborates the Anti-Corruption Layer requirement with worked examples: Kubernetes Deployment -> Adapter -> Runtime Observation (not a direct object-model mapping); Nexus Repository/Blob Store/Component/Asset/Version -> Adapter -> KnowledgeOS Artifact/ArtifactVersion/ArtifactObservation; Git commit/branch/tag/repository/merge -> Commit->ImplementationEvidence without redefining Git's domain; CI 'Pipeline #842 passed' -> VerificationEvidence while the CI system remains authority for its own execution (KnowledgeOS ≠ CI/CD)." - [S1028] types=[FORMALIZATION, PRINCIPLE] scope=CROSS-OBJECT — "Places Claude/Codex at the application/integration layer, consuming governed context and producing evidence/recommendations/actions; states the agent must not become an upstream context (Agent ↛ Governance meaning 'agent determines governance truth' is forbidden; correct is Agent->Recommendation->Governance, agent downstream from authority); requires a recommendation to carry producedBy=Agent, basedOn=Evidence, proposedFor=Decision, making the AI contribution explicit without granting authority; both Claude and Codex should consume the same KnowledgeOSContext (Context Contract) even though harnesses differ operationally, giving the correct symmetry SameKnowledgeAuthority+SameEvidenceDiscipline+SameGovernanceBoundary+SameActionConstraints, explicitly not SameConfigurationFiles." (anchor: "KnowledgeOS → Context Projection → AI Agent → {Analysis, Tools→{Git,CI,Runtime}}")
- [S1028] types=[PRINCIPLE] scope=THEORY-LEVEL — "Formulates the dependency-direction rule (Governance->Knowledge->Assurance->Engineering, with evidence flowing back Engineering->Observation->Evidence->Knowledge/Governance) and three named forbidden-dependency anti-patterns: (1) Runtime->'current reality'->automatically authoritative knowledge->Governance is forbidden because observation ('what is') does not establish organizational intent ('what should be'); (2) Agent->Inference->Authoritative Architecture is forbidden, correct is Agent->Inference->Evidence->Validation->Governance->Authority; (3) Assurance->Violation->automatic policy change is forbidden, correct is Assurance->Finding->Governance->Decision."
